action_taken: Emitted as a bounded follow-up finding (NEW-210). The V5 closures themselves were left fail-closed rather than being redesigned around the waiver system, because no executing consumer of the waiver system exists to bypass today.
finding: The contract's waiver model has a single boolean per profile (allows_waived) and a required-fields list that is about PROCESS (identifier, owner, evidence, rationale, expiration). It has no notion of gate CLASS, so it cannot distinguish a waivable quality deviation from a non-waivable identity/integrity defect.
mitigating_facts: V5 introduced explicit fail-closed identity gates that do not consult the contract at all: finalize_run_pack (D16), strict provenance (D17) and the candidate identity pre-runtime gate (E24) all fail closed independently of any waiver record.
runtime_certified sets allows_waived: false, so runtime certification cannot be waived.
residual_exposure: Gates that would be evaluated purely through the contract (none of which currently has an executing consumer) remain unclassified.
risk: Because production_candidate sets allows_waived: true and the contract has no classifier, a waiver could in principle be attached to an identity or integrity gate such as map_registry_identity or deterministic_provenance, converting a genuine integrity defect into a passing release.

waiver_schema.rule: No anonymous warning suppression. A gate with unresolved FAIL/INCOMPLETE status and no matching waiver record blocks the profile it's required for.
